issues.legal_issue: A default term in a compromise is not penal when it only removes a special bargain available to a party who fails to pay the agreed price on time.
material_facts: A compromise gave one party the option to acquire part of the other parties’ share for an agreed price, payable by specified deadlines.
The property’s market value was substantially higher than the agreed price.
The compromise provided that failure to pay on time would leave the original partition decree in force, thereby depriving the purchaser of the special opportunity to acquire the share.
The purchaser sought to retain the other benefits of the compromise while avoiding the default term.
issues.conclusion: The default term was not penal or illegal and could not be ignored on that ground.
issues.legal_principle: The court rejected the argument under Section 74 of the Indian Contract Act. A penalty involves punishment; a term that merely deprives a party of a special advantage for failing to meet the condition for obtaining it is not a penalty. The court did not rely on an earlier case for this conclusion.

predicates.compromise_term_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether a default term in a court-recorded compromise should be disregarded.
predicates.agreement_offered_special_purchase_barga: The agreement gave a party an opportunity to acquire another party’s property interest on agreed terms.
predicates.payment_deadline_was_condition_of_bargai: The agreement made timely payment a condition for obtaining the property interest.
predicates.default_only_removed_purchase_opportunit: Failure to pay on time deprived the party only of the opportunity to obtain the property interest, rather than imposing a punishment.

issues.definition: When a compromise offers a special purchase bargain conditional on timely payment and default only removes that opportunity, the default term is not penal.

issues.legal_issue: A court should not grant a grossly delayed extension of a payment deadline in a compromise decree where the circumstances show that doing so would be unjust.
material_facts: A compromise recorded in an appellate proceeding allowed a party to acquire part of the other parties’ share by paying in instalments by fixed dates.
The first instalment was paid, but the remaining amount was not paid by the deadline.
The party applied for an extension more than a year and a half after the missed deadline.
The court had previously permitted the other parties to refund the first instalment after the default, and the defaulting party had obtained extensions but failed to comply with directions.
The agreed price was substantially below the market value of the property, and the court found that justice favored the parties seeking to enforce the deadline.
issues.conclusion: The extension was unjustified; the order granting it was set aside and the application for more time was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: Even where a court has power to extend time under a compromise, it should not do so liberally: under Smt. Periyakkal v. Smt. Dakshyani, time is not ordinarily extended or extended merely on request, but may be extended in rare cases to prevent manifest injustice. The court found that the circumstances favored enforcing the deadline and that the term was not a forfeiture clause. It did not decide the abstract question of the court’s general power to alter a consent order.

rule.if: extension_request_in_consent_decree_case and payment_was_grossly_delayed and prior_noncompliance_was_recorded and (special_bargain_was_below_market_value or justice_favored_enforcing_deadline)

predicates.extension_request_in_consent_decree_case: A party in a proceeding concerning a court-recorded compromise asks the court to extend a payment deadline in that compromise.
predicates.payment_was_grossly_delayed: The party sought more time only after a substantial delay beyond the agreed payment deadline.
predicates.prior_noncompliance_was_recorded: The court record showed that the party had previously failed to comply with payment or court directions.
predicates.special_bargain_was_below_market_value: The agreement gave the party an opportunity to acquire a property interest for less than its market value.
predicates.justice_favored_enforcing_deadline: The circumstances showed that enforcing the agreed deadline favored the party entitled to receive payment.

issues.definition: When a party seeks a grossly late extension under a compromise decree, has a record of noncompliance, and the circumstances favor enforcing the deadline, the extension should be denied.

issues.legal_issue: A party must receive reasonable notice and an opportunity to contest an application to extend a deadline when the party’s former counsel has disclaimed authority to act for them.
material_facts: After the appeal had been disposed of on compromise, one party applied to extend the deadline for a remaining payment.
The parties entitled to receive payment said their former counsel no longer represented them and asked that notice be sent directly to them.
No direct notice was sent, and the application was listed for consideration shortly afterward.
The court nevertheless considered and granted the extension application.
issues.conclusion: The complaint that the parties were not given a reasonable opportunity to contest the application was well founded; the court did not remand because it had resolved the merits.
issues.legal_principle: The affected parties should have been given reasonable notice of the extension application, particularly after their former counsel said that he lacked authority to represent them and requested direct service. The judgment states no statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for this procedural conclusion.

rule.if: post_compromise_extension_proceeding and former_counsel_disclaimed_authority and direct_notice_was_requested and affected_parties_received_no_direct_notice

predicates.post_compromise_extension_proceeding: A party seeks an extension after the underlying appeal has been disposed of by compromise.
predicates.former_counsel_disclaimed_authority: The affected parties’ former lawyer told the court that he no longer had authority to represent them.
predicates.direct_notice_was_requested: The former lawyer asked the court to send notice of the application directly to the affected parties.
predicates.affected_parties_received_no_direct_noti: The court considered the application without directly notifying the affected parties.

issues.definition: When an extension application is made after a compromise and former counsel disclaims authority while requesting direct notice, considering the application without directly notifying the affected parties makes the notice opportunity inadequate.
